analysis: Examined three changes. (1) New ServingReadiness.swift (lines 1-178) is a read-only diagnostics function that maps DaemonState to a verdict (authorized, pending or blocked) with operator advice. It does not grant or deny routing; the file header says the coordinator owns authorization. It reads coordinatorConnection, addonHold, trust, authorization and appAttest from the daemon state file. The 'authorized' verdicts at lines 62, 65 and 68 are display-only. Line 62 reports 'hardware-trusted (legacy verification)' when no authorization object is present and trustLevel is 'hardware'. That could overstate readiness for a coordinator whose policy differs, but it is advisory text, consistent with T-052 only if no code treats the verdict as permission. This needs checking in the callers. The advice text interpolates coordinator-supplied reason strings (lines 113, 122, 125). These are shown on the CLI, so a hostile or compromised coordinator could inject terminal control characters or long text. The coordinator is trusted in this model, and the state file is owner-only, so no finding is reported. Line 149 shows an install command built from BuildEnvironment.coordinatorHTTPURL and piped to bash. It is only advice text and uses a build-time constant. (2) ProviderLogger.swift adds three fixed enum cases (lines 147-149) to the closed public log vocabulary. They carry no associated values and no request-derived data, so the public-log privacy contract is preserved. (3) ProviderLoop+Capacity.swift line 82 adds a call to superviseServingAuthorization() in capacityRefreshTick. Its implementation was not supplied. The log message 'has not authorized this connection for at least 15 min; re-registering it' implies that the supervisor triggers re-registration or reconnect. Questions for deeper review: whether the re-registration path can be abused (a coordinator holding a provider in an unauthorized state could cause a reconnect loop), whether it interacts with the T-053 endpoint-replacement and nonce binding, whether it respects add-on holds (TB-012 and T-059), and whether it is rate-limited. Without that source, no concrete regression can be asserted.
